title: Ten-bit color on a Linux screen

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Most screens show eight bits per color channel. What happens when you give them ten?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's what this small experiment explores. Antoine loads image data into a GTK drawing area through Cairo.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And the trick is in the pixel format?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. A script called Viewer3 makes it explicit: each channel sample is masked and packed into one thirty-two-bit number, then used to build an RGB thirty surface.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So you see exactly how ten-bit pixels are laid out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right, and it's a handy way to test color banding and brightness curves on Linux display servers. The Python code is short, which makes it easy to read. The written page walks through it.
